Title: Platform administrator signs in to the control plane
Preconditions: PLATFORM_URL, PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAIL and PLATFORM_ADMIN_PASSWORD set in .env; no existing platform session
Steps: 1) Open PLATFORM_URL; 2) Enter PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAIL in the email field; 3) Enter PLATFORM_ADMIN_PASSWORD; 4) Activate 'Sign in'
Expected Result: POST /api/v1/auth/login returns 200; a session is established and the console exposes the 'Universities' nav item or the 'University management' heading
Notes: Covered by tests/web/platform/university-bootstrap.spec.ts step 1 and 01-platform-admin.md PAC-01 in tests/web/testcases/platform-admin.spec.ts

Title: Wrong platform password is refused
Preconditions: Valid platform email with a deliberately wrong password
Steps: 1) Open PLATFORM_URL; 2) Submit the valid email with a wrong password; 3) Inspect the response and the rendered page
Expected Result: Login returns 401; no authenticated console renders; the operator stays on the sign-in form
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-02 in tests/web/testcases/platform-admin.spec.ts. The refusal copy on the platform origin has not been captured; assert status and absence of a session only

Title: Unknown platform account is not disclosed
Preconditions: An email address that was never registered on the control plane
Steps: 1) Submit an unregistered email with any password; 2) Inspect the status and the body
Expected Result: 401 or 422 and the body never states that the account does not exist
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-03 asserts 'no such user' is absent. Extend the negative phrase list once the platform console copy is captured

Title: Empty credentials never authenticate
Steps: 1) Open PLATFORM_URL; 2) Submit with an empty email and an empty password
Expected Result: Either native validation blocks submission or the request is answered 400/401/422; no session is created
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-04

Title: Whitespace around the email is handled deterministically
Steps: 1) Submit the email wrapped in leading and trailing spaces with the correct password; 2) Read the outcome
Expected Result: Either the value is trimmed and the operator signs in, or it is refused with a validation message; a 5xx is a failure
Notes: Trimming behaviour on the platform origin has not been observed; capture the outgoing request body and the response before automating

Title: Device-tagged login body yields a browser-parity session
Preconditions: The console login body was captured once from a real sign-in
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/auth/login with email, password, device_id, device_label, platform and browser; 2) Read the issued cookies; 3) GET /api/v1/enterprise/tenants
Expected Result: 200; session cookies are issued and the tenants read returns 200
Test Data: device_id random UUID; device_label 'Win32 Platform Bootstrap'; platform Win32; browser 'Playwright Platform Bootstrap'
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts sends exactly this body so the platform issues the same session a browser receives

Title: Anonymous tenant list is refused
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/tenants with no cookies
Expected Result: 401 or 403 and no tenant metadata in the body
Notes: Extends 01-platform-admin.md PAC-16 to the read path

Title: Platform session cookie attributes are safe
Steps: 1) Sign in and record the raw Set-Cookie header; 2) Inspect HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and Domain
Expected Result: The session cookie is HttpOnly and Secure with a restrictive SameSite; Domain is host-only for the console host unless a documented shared-domain design exists
Notes: Playwright storageState does not expose cookie attributes, so read Set-Cookie directly. A cookie scoped to PLATFORM_BASE_DOMAIN is sent to every tenant host and must be escalated (see PAC-122)

Title: Control-plane session is not reused as a tenant session
Preconditions: A signed-in platform session and a reachable tenant host
Steps: 1) Sign in on PLATFORM_URL; 2) Load the tenant host in the same browser context; 3) Inspect which cookies the tenant host receives and whether it renders a tenant shell unauthenticated
Expected Result: The tenant workspace demands its own credentials; the platform session does not authenticate a tenant
Notes: pages/PlatformAdminPage.ts states the platform reuses the DVS session auth while the console shell is separate. Confirm cookie scope; escalate if a tenant host accepts the platform session

Title: Platform identity is readable from the session
Steps: 1) Sign in; 2) GET /api/v1/auth/me on the platform origin
Expected Result: 200 with a body identifying the signed-in platform account; no tenant workspace role is returned
Notes: Only status and identity presence can be asserted; the platform /auth/me payload shape has not been captured. Extend the assertion once it is snapshotted

Title: Signing out ends the platform session
Steps: 1) Sign in; 2) Activate the sign-out control; 3) Re-request /api/v1/enterprise/tenants
Expected Result: The console returns to sign-in and the next tenants request is 401 or 403
Notes: Sign out is verified on the tenant shell but the console sign-out control has not been captured. Confirm the label and that it revokes the server session, not only the client cookie

Title: Provisioning without a CSRF token is refused
Preconditions: Authenticated platform session with a csrftoken cookie
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants with a valid body and no X-CSRFToken header; 2) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: 403 refusal and no new university in the list
Test Data: Valid create body, CSRF header omitted
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts always sends X-CSRFToken read from the csrftoken cookie, which evidences CSRF protection on control-plane writes. Confirm the exact status

Title: Forged CSRF token is refused
Steps: 1) POST tenants with X-CSRFToken set to a fabricated value; 2) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: 403 and the list is unchanged
Notes: Same protection as PAC-012 with a different attack input

Title: Unknown create fields cannot escalate privileges
Steps: 1) POST tenants including extra keys such as role, is_staff, is_superuser, id and institution_id; 2) Read the response; 3) Sign in as the created administrator and read /api/v1/auth/me
Expected Result: The extra keys are ignored or rejected and the new administrator holds only the standard university administrator role
Test Data: Valid body plus hostile extra keys
Notes: TenantProvisionIn documents only name, code, admin_*, subdomain, plan, enabled_modules, data_region and branding/AI fields. Record whether unknown keys are rejected or dropped, then assert no escalation

Title: Oversized and Unicode passwords fail gracefully
Steps: 1) Submit a 512-character password; 2) Submit a password containing emoji and right-to-left characters
Expected Result: 400/401/422 with no 5xx and no session created
Notes: No platform password policy has been observed. The no-5xx assertion is automatable immediately; the policy outcome must be captured first

Title: Whitespace-only university name is rejected
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants with name set to three spaces; 2) Read the response; 3) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: 4xx field error and no university is created with a blank name
Notes: A blank university name renders an unidentifiable tenant in the console and on the handover sheet

Title: Platform Universities nav opens the university management view
Steps: 1) Activate the 'Platform' nav group; 2) Activate the 'Universities' item
Expected Result: The 'University management' view renders with the 'Super Admin' eyebrow
Notes: pages/PlatformAdminPage.ts openUniversities(); the nav item is matched as a button or a link

Title: Console lands authenticated after sign-in
Steps: 1) Sign in; 2) Observe the landing surface
Expected Result: The console lands with the 'Universities' nav item or the 'University management' heading visible and no second sign-in prompt
Notes: PlatformAdminPage.login() accepts either surface, which evidences that both are reachable after authentication

Title: Reloading the console keeps the session
Preconditions: A signed-in platform session on the university view
Steps: 1) Open Universities; 2) Reload the console page
Expected Result: Still authenticated; 'University management' renders again without a sign-in prompt
Notes: Reload behaviour on the control plane has not been captured; tenant-shell parity is plausible but unproven

Title: Tenant workspaces are not exposed on the console
Steps: 1) Sign in; 2) Inspect the full navigation inventory
Expected Result: Only the 'Universities' module is exposed; tenant modules such as 'Exam configuration', 'Marking schemes', 'Access governance', 'Evaluation desk' and 'Digitization' are absent
Notes: utils/dvsRoles.ts declares PLATFORM_ROLES modules as Universities only and keeps platform roles out of the tenant login matrix

Title: Back and forward navigation keeps the console usable
Steps: 1) Open Universities; 2) Press Back; 3) Press Forward
Expected Result: The console returns to the university management view with no session loss and no error screen
Notes: Single-page-app routing on the platform origin has not been captured. Confirm the behaviour before automating

Title: Console document title identifies the control plane
Steps: 1) Sign in; 2) Read document.title
Expected Result: A stable product-specific title that distinguishes the console from a tenant workspace (the tenant shell uses ADMIEZO | Evaluation Operations)
Notes: Capture the platform document title; it is unverified and must not be guessed

Title: Tenant list is readable
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/tenants
Expected Result: 200 with a JSON array; every row exposes id, name and code
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-05 asserts id, name and code on the first five rows. The role file also names a kind field, which is reconciled in PAC-028

Title: Listed universities are unique
Steps: 1) GET tenants; 2) Collect every id and every code
Expected Result: No duplicate id and no duplicate code across the list
Notes: A duplicated row would corrupt the nextUniversityNumber() sequence in utils/platformClient.ts

Title: A provisioned university appears exactly once
Preconditions: A university created earlier in this run
Steps: 1) Re-read the tenant list; 2) Count rows with the created code; 3) Compare the row id with the create response id
Expected Result: Exactly one row, and its id equals the id returned by provisioning
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-07

Title: Tenant list rows carry metadata only
Steps: 1) GET tenants; 2) Inspect the key set of every row
Expected Result: Rows carry tenant metadata such as id, name, code, hostname, administrator email and institution linkage only; no candidate, script, paper or marking data
Notes: The tenant list is the control plane broadest data surface. Assert an allow-list of keys so a future field addition cannot leak tenant business data

Title: Row scope fields are present and stable
Steps: 1) GET tenants; 2) Inspect one live row and compare its keys with the documented contract
Expected Result: The documented row contract and the live row agree, including any kind or module-scope field
Notes: The role document expects a kind field while utils/platformClient.ts never reads it. Capture one live row and reconcile the documentation before asserting

Title: Tenant list scales to a large estate
Preconditions: An estate with at least 200 universities
Steps: 1) Time five sequential tenant-list reads; 2) Record payload size and row count
Expected Result: Every call returns 200 with the complete estate inside the configured expect timeout; no truncation and no pagination error
Notes: The route constant carries no pagination or filter parameters, so the list appears unpaginated. Measure the real estate size and p95 latency before setting a budget; escalate if the payload exceeds a few MB

Title: University list can be narrowed at scale
Preconditions: A large estate in the console
Steps: 1) Open Universities; 2) Look for a search or filter control over name and code
Expected Result: The operator can locate a university by name or code without scanning every row; if no control exists, record the usability gap
Notes: pages/PlatformAdminPage.ts captures only the heading, the nav item and the New university action. Confirm the absence before filing it; do not invent a control

Title: Repeated list reads are stable
Steps: 1) GET tenants twice; 2) Compare the id set and the ordering
Expected Result: The same id set both times and a deterministic ordering
Notes: Ordering stability matters because automation derives the next university number from the list

Title: Concurrent list reads never return an error page
Steps: 1) Issue 20 concurrent GET tenants; 2) Validate status, content type and JSON parse
Expected Result: Every response is 200 with a JSON content type and a parseable array; no HTML error page
Notes: Control-plane concurrency limits are unverified. If 429 appears, record the documented rate limit rather than treating it as a failure

Title: A university is provisioned from the console
Steps: 1) Open Platform and then Universities; 2) Activate 'New university'; 3) Fill university name and code, Administrator first name, Administrator last name and Administrator email; 4) Activate 'Provision university'
Expected Result: The create request returns 2xx and the 'Administrator handover' sheet renders on the console
Test Data: name Automation testing -N; code automation-testing-N; administrator Automation University Admin; email automation.testing.N@example.com
Notes: Headed flow driven by npm run test:platform. Arm PlatformAdminPage.waitForProvisionResponse before the operator acts so the response is never missed

Title: Create response carries the full handover contract
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants with the documented body; 2) Inspect the JSON
Expected Result: 200 with id, name, code, hostname, admin_email, admin_user_id and temporary_password
Test Data: name, code, admin_email, admin_first_name, admin_last_name, plan
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts provisionUniversity() reads exactly these keys and throws when hostname or temporary_password is missing

Title: Created university is linked to an institution
Preconditions: A university created in this run
Steps: 1) Read institution_id from the create response; 2) GET /api/v1/enterprise/institutions
Expected Result: institution_id is non-empty and the institution list contains that id
Notes: The client reads institution_id but the linkage has never been asserted. Capture the institutions payload shape first

Title: Provisioning success status is stable
Steps: 1) Provision and record the HTTP status code
Expected Result: The console path returns 200 on success; a different 2xx is reported so waitForProvisionResponse cannot mask a contract change
Notes: Both the spec and the client assume 200, while waitForProvisionResponse accepts any 2xx. Asserting the code keeps the contract honest

Title: Tenant URL derives from the shared base domain
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Resolve https://hostname; 3) Open it
Expected Result: The URL resolves under PLATFORM_BASE_DOMAIN and serves the tenant sign-in surface
Notes: university-bootstrap.spec.ts asserts tenantUrl equals https plus hostname

Title: Optional subdomain governs the hostname
Steps: 1) Provision with subdomain dvs-pac-runId; 2) Read hostname; 3) Open the derived URL
Expected Result: hostname is subdomain.PLATFORM_BASE_DOMAIN and the tenant URL opens
Notes: subdomain is listed in TenantProvisionIn but its effect on hostname has not been captured; utils/platformClient.ts only falls back to it when hostname is absent

Title: Plan is accepted and persisted
Steps: 1) Provision with plan enterprise; 2) Re-read the university row
Expected Result: The create succeeds and the plan is visible in the console or the tenant record
Notes: plan is accepted by the serializer and sent by utils/platformClient.ts, but no response field or console column carrying it is documented

Title: enabled_modules at creation governs tenant module access
Preconditions: A fresh university created with an explicit module subset
Steps: 1) Provision with an explicit enabled_modules subset; 2) Sign in as the new administrator; 3) Inspect the tenant navigation
Expected Result: Only the enabled modules are offered to the tenant administrator
Notes: enabled_modules is documented in TenantProvisionIn; its key format and enforcement are unverified

Title: data_region is accepted and recorded
Steps: 1) Provision with an explicit data_region; 2) Look for the region in the control plane
Expected Result: The region is accepted and can be evidenced for data-residency review
Notes: data_region is listed in TenantProvisionIn; the allowed values and any residency control are unverified

Title: Branding fields are accepted at creation
Steps: 1) Provision with branding values; 2) Complete the administrator first login; 3) Inspect the tenant banner
Expected Result: Branding is accepted and applied to the tenant workspace, or the request is rejected with a clear message if branding is unsupported
Notes: Section 0.1 mentions branding and AI fields without naming them; capture the accepted keys before testing

Title: Duplicate university code is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants with the same code but a fresh name and administrator email; 2) Read the list
Expected Result: 4xx validation error naming the code, and the estate still holds one university with that code
Test Data: Existing code plus fresh name and email
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-12. The platform returns 200 for a successful create, so any 2xx here is a defect

Title: Missing university name is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants without name
Expected Result: 4xx and nothing is created
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-13

Title: Missing administrator email is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants with name and code only
Expected Result: 4xx and nothing is created
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-14

Title: Malformed administrator email is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants with admin_email set to not-an-email
Expected Result: 4xx and nothing is created
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-15

Title: Missing university code is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants with name and administrator email only
Expected Result: 4xx and no university is created; no code is invented on the caller behalf
Notes: code is a documented required field but the missing-code case is not covered by the existing suite. Confirm both the error and the absence of a server-generated code

Title: Missing administrator name is rejected
Steps: 1) POST tenants without admin_first_name and admin_last_name
Expected Result: 4xx and no administrator is created without a name
Notes: Both names are documented request fields; the validation behaviour is unverified

Title: Empty strings are treated as missing
Steps: 1) POST tenants with name, code and admin_email set to empty strings
Expected Result: 4xx with field-level errors and nothing created
Notes: Distinguishes required-field validation from presence-only validation

Title: University code format is validated
Steps: 1) POST tenants with codes containing a space, uppercase letters, an underscore, a slash and a single character
Expected Result: Each code is either rejected with a field error or normalized to a hostname-safe form; no 5xx and no unresolvable tenant URL
Test Data: Candidate codes a b, AbC, a_b, a/b, a
Notes: The code becomes part of the hostname, so an unsafe code is a routing risk

Title: University code length boundaries
Steps: 1) Provision with a 1-character code; 2) Provision with 63-character and 64-character codes
Expected Result: Accepted values produce a resolvable hostname and rejected values return a 4xx field error
Notes: DNS label limits imply a 63-character ceiling; the serializer limit is unverified

Title: University name length boundary
Steps: 1) Provision with a 255-character name; 2) Read the stored name from the list
Expected Result: Accepted or rejected with a clear message; never a 5xx and never a silently truncated name
Notes: Truncation would be a data-integrity defect in reports and certificates

Title: Administrator email reuse across universities
Steps: 1) Provision university A with email X; 2) Provision university B with the same email X; 3) Compare the two handovers
Expected Result: The second request is refused, or it creates an independent administrator in B with no shared credentials
Notes: Reusing one mailbox for administrators in two tenants is a separation risk. Assert only that credentials are never shared silently

Title: Email case and Unicode are handled consistently
Preconditions: A university provisioned with a mixed-case email
Steps: 1) Provision with Administrator@Example.COM; 2) Retry with administrator@example.com
Expected Result: Both attempts behave identically: the second is refused as a duplicate or both are accepted as distinct
Notes: Behaviour must be identical in both directions or the duplicate rule is bypassable by case

Title: Type-confused login payload is refused
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/auth/login with password sent as an array; 2) Repeat with email sent as an object
Expected Result: 400 or 422 with no 5xx and no session created
Test Data: password as an array; email as an object
Notes: Serializer type confusion is a classic 5xx crash path. Assert only the 4xx family and the absence of a session

Title: Content type is enforced
Steps: 1) POST tenants as application/x-www-form-urlencoded; 2) POST the same body as text/plain
Expected Result: 4xx client error; no 5xx and no university created
Notes: A form-encoded body that silently succeeds would bypass the JSON schema

Title: Unicode university name is stored intact
Steps: 1) Provision with a name containing Devanagari, accented Latin and an emoji; 2) Read the name back from the list and from the tenant banner
Expected Result: The stored name matches the input character for character
Notes: Institution names are user-visible in the tenant banner, so mojibake is a real production defect

Title: Anonymous provisioning is refused
Steps: 1) POST tenants with a valid body and no cookies; 2) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: 401 or 403 and no university appears in the list
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-16

Title: Tenant administrator cannot provision a university
Steps: 1) Sign in on the tenant; 2) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants on the tenant origin; 3) Repeat on the platform origin without a platform session
Expected Result: Both attempts are refused (401/403/404) and no university is created
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-17 covers the read path; this covers the write path, which is the higher-impact attack

Title: Provisioning completes inside the configured budget
Steps: 1) Time the create request from submit to response; 2) Compare with the budget
Expected Result: A university is created inside PLATFORM_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_MS and the console shows the handover without a timeout
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-27. Record the actual duration so a slow-provisioning regression is visible rather than absorbed by a generous budget

Title: Concurrent creates with the same code yield one university
Steps: 1) Fire two identical create requests in parallel; 2) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: Exactly one success; the other is a 4xx conflict; the list holds one row for that code
Notes: Duplicate protection under concurrency is unverified; a double success would create two tenants competing for one hostname

Title: Idempotency-key replay does not duplicate a university
Steps: 1) Create with a fixed Idempotency-Key; 2) Replay the identical request and key; 3) Read the list
Expected Result: One university only; the replay returns the original result or a clear conflict
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts sets a fresh Idempotency-Key on every write, which evidences the header is part of the protocol, but replay protection has never been asserted. This is the main duplicate-provisioning risk

Title: An aborted client does not leave an invisible university
Steps: 1) Send a create request and abort the client well below PLATFORM_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_MS; 2) Wait past the budget; 3) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: At most one university exists for the code and it is discoverable in the list; no half-provisioned orphan tenant
Notes: Slow or aborted provisioning is the documented production risk; capture whether the server completes or rolls back the transaction

Title: Console recovers from a rejected create
Preconditions: The console open on the provisioning form
Steps: 1) Submit a duplicate code; 2) Read the error; 3) Resubmit with a unique code
Expected Result: The error is shown for the submitted form, no phantom row appears, and the retry creates exactly one university
Notes: Assert the estate list, not only the on-screen message

Title: Control plane survives a malformed JSON body
Steps: 1) POST tenants with the body not-json; 2) Send a valid create afterwards
Expected Result: Status below 500 and the next valid request succeeds normally
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-29

Title: Oversized create payload is refused
Steps: 1) POST tenants with a 1 MB name and a 1 MB branding blob
Expected Result: 4xx (400 or 413) or an explicit size error; no 5xx and no partial university
Notes: A partial university from an oversized body would be hard to clean up because no delete route is documented

Title: Each run provisions a distinct university
Steps: 1) Run the provisioning flow twice; 2) Compare id, code, hostname and administrator email
Expected Result: All four values differ between runs; no run reuses a previous university
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-11. nextUniversityNumber() computes the sequence from the live list

Title: Three rapid provisions stay independent
Steps: 1) Provision three universities back to back; 2) Compare ids, hostnames and temporary passwords
Expected Result: Three distinct tenants and three distinct handovers with no cross-contamination of response bodies
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-28

Title: Provisioning does not mutate existing universities
Preconditions: A tenant list snapshot taken before provisioning
Steps: 1) Snapshot id, code and name for every existing row; 2) Provision a new university; 3) Re-read the list and diff
Expected Result: Only the new row is added; every pre-existing row is unchanged
Notes: A side-effecting create would silently rename or re-host an unrelated university

Title: Handover delivers email, password and tenant URL
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Inspect the response and the visible sheet
Expected Result: Administrator email, temporary password and tenant URL are all delivered, and 'Administrator handover', 'Copy temporary password' and 'Open university workspace' are present
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-09. PlatformAdminPage.readVisibleHandover() is the DOM fallback when the response is redacted

Title: Copy temporary password copies the exact value
Preconditions: The handover sheet visible after provisioning
Steps: 1) Activate 'Copy temporary password'; 2) Read the clipboard; 3) Sign in on the tenant URL with the copied value
Expected Result: The clipboard matches the delivered password exactly and the tenant accepts it
Notes: Clipboard reads need browser permission. Compare length and character classes; never print the value

Title: Open university workspace reaches the new tenant
Preconditions: The handover sheet visible after provisioning
Steps: 1) Activate 'Open university workspace'
Expected Result: The new tenant sign-in page loads on the URL derived from hostname; the platform console is not shown
Notes: Confirms the handover link is a tenant URL and not a console self-reference

Title: Handover is shown once per provisioning
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Provision and note the temporary password; 2) Navigate away from the handover; 3) Re-open the created university from the list
Expected Result: The temporary password is not displayed again anywhere in the console
Notes: Section 0.1 states the handover is shown once. Confirm the console offers no re-reveal, because a stored one-time password breaks the single-use model

Title: One-time password satisfies the tenant password policy
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Measure the length and character classes of the delivered password
Expected Result: At least 12 characters with mixed case, digits and symbols so the tenant Set your password screen can accept a replacement without a second reset
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-18 asserts 12 or more characters and mixed characters. The authoritative policy lives in the tenant Access governance policy

Title: Consecutive handovers use distinct secrets
Steps: 1) Provision twice; 2) Compare the two temporary passwords and the two admin_user_ids
Expected Result: Both differ; no reuse of a previous one-time password or administrator id
Notes: Random generation is expected but has never been asserted; identical values indicate a reused or predictable secret

Title: Temporary password is never persisted by automation
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Inspect .env and the run-state file; 3) Search the working tree for the value
Expected Result: The temporary password appears in neither file and in no tracked file
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-10. university-bootstrap.spec.ts asserts .env explicitly

Title: Update with an empty body changes nothing
Preconditions: A university created in this run
Steps: 1) PATCH /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenantId} with an empty object; 2) Re-read the row
Expected Result: 4xx, or a 200 that is a strict no-op; name, code, hostname and administrator email are unchanged
Notes: A partial-update serializer that treats missing fields as blank would wipe the university details

Title: Handover administrator email matches the request
Preconditions: A provisioning request with a known administrator email
Steps: 1) Provision with a chosen email; 2) Compare response admin_email with the request
Expected Result: Identical value with no rewriting or truncation
Notes: A rewritten email would send the handover to a mailbox the operator does not control

Title: Handover administrator id identifies the created user
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Sign in on the tenant as the new administrator; 3) GET /api/v1/auth/me and compare user id with admin_user_id
Expected Result: The same numeric user id and an administrator role
Notes: The tenant /auth/me payload exposes user.id; the platform admin_user_id mapping has never been cross-checked

Title: Handover password is masked until deliberately revealed
Preconditions: The handover sheet visible after provisioning
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Inspect how the temporary password is rendered
Expected Result: The value is masked by default or held in a read-only field behind an explicit reveal or copy action; it is not plain page text captured by any screenshot
Notes: readVisibleHandover() handles both text and readonly-input rendering, which evidences that both renderings occur. Confirm which is current

Title: Audit limit accepts only integers
Steps: 1) GET the audit path with limit=abc; 2) limit=1.5; 3) limit= empty
Expected Result: 4xx for each, or a documented fallback to the default limit; no 5xx and no unbounded payload
Notes: Assert the status is below 500 and the payload stays bounded

Title: An unused handover password expires
Preconditions: A university provisioned but never activated
Steps: 1) Provision; 2) Wait beyond the stated expiry, or read Expires where the sheet shows it; 3) Sign in with the temporary password
Expected Result: An expired handover password is refused and the operator must issue a reset
Notes: Section 10 documents an Expires field for tenant user provisioning; whether the platform-issued administrator handover carries an expiry is unverified

Title: New administrator signs in with the handover password
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Open the tenant URL; 2) Sign in with the handover email and temporary password
Expected Result: 200 with must_change_password true and the Set your password screen renders
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-22

Title: The handover password can be replaced
Preconditions: The Set your password screen for the new administrator
Steps: 1) Fill New password and Confirm password; 2) Activate Set password and continue
Expected Result: POST /api/v1/auth/password/complete-setup returns ok true and the authenticated shell renders
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-23

Title: The handover password stops working after replacement
Steps: 1) Sign out; 2) Sign in with the temporary password
Expected Result: 401; the one-time password is consumed
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-25. DVS_VERIFY_TEMP_REUSE gates the extra failed login

Title: The permanent password grants the administrator role
Steps: 1) Sign in with the permanent password; 2) GET /api/v1/auth/me
Expected Result: 200 with an administrator role inside the provisioned tenant
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-24 and 01-platform-admin.md PAC-26

Title: Tenant banner shows the provisioned university name
Steps: 1) Sign in on the new tenant; 2) Read the banner tenant name
Expected Result: The banner shows the name submitted at provisioning and matches DVS_TENANT_NAME
Notes: persistUniversityRuntime() records the provisioned name for exactly this assertion

Title: Handover password is not bound to the provisioning device
Preconditions: A university provisioned in browser context A
Steps: 1) Provision in context A; 2) Sign in with the handover password from an unrelated context B
Expected Result: The first login succeeds from context B, proving the secret is not device- or session-bound
Notes: The platform login body carries device_id and device_label, so confirm the handover secret itself is device-independent. Support engineers routinely complete handover from another machine

Title: University details can be updated
Preconditions: A university created in this run; a signed-in platform session
Steps: 1) PATCH /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenantId} with a changed name; 2) Re-read the tenant list
Expected Result: 2xx and the list shows the new value exactly once
Notes: The PATCH route is observed but its patchable fields and response shape are undocumented. Capture the accepted keys before asserting

Title: Unknown tenant id is refused on update
Steps: 1) PATCH /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/nonexistent-runId with a name change; 2) Read the list
Expected Result: 404 or 403 and no other tenant is modified
Notes: Confirms the update route is keyed by tenant id and cannot be retargeted

Title: Invalid plan value is refused on update
Preconditions: A university with a persisted plan
Steps: 1) PATCH tenants/{tenantId} with plan not-a-plan; 2) Re-read the row
Expected Result: 4xx field error and the stored plan is unchanged
Notes: Depends on PAC-039 confirming that plan is persisted and readable

Title: University update requires a session
Steps: 1) PATCH tenants/{tenantId} with no cookies
Expected Result: 401 or 403 and nothing changes
Notes: Only the read and create paths are covered by current automation

Title: University update requires a CSRF token
Steps: 1) PATCH /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenantId} with a session but no X-CSRFToken; 2) Re-read the row
Expected Result: 403 and nothing changes
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts documents the csrftoken header as required on every write, which encompasses PATCH; confirm the exact status

Title: Administrator password reset issues a new handover
Preconditions: A disposable university created only for this case
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenantId}/administrator/reset-password; 2) Read the response; 3) Sign in on the tenant with the new password
Expected Result: A new one-time password is delivered once and the tenant accepts it with must_change_password true
Notes: The route is observed but its request body and response fields are not. Never run this against a university whose permanent password the running workflow still needs

Title: Reset revokes the previous administrator password
Preconditions: A disposable university with a known permanent password
Steps: 1) Reset the administrator password; 2) Sign in with the previous permanent password
Expected Result: 401; only the newest password works
Notes: A reset that leaves the old password valid defeats account recovery

Title: Two consecutive resets leave only the latest password valid
Steps: 1) Reset twice; 2) Test both issued passwords
Expected Result: The second reset invalidates the first and exactly one password works
Notes: Two live one-time secrets per administrator is a takeover risk if both stay valid

Title: Codes that differ only by case cannot collide
Steps: 1) Provision with code AbC-runId; 2) Provision with code abc-runId; 3) Read the tenant list
Expected Result: The second request is refused as a duplicate, or both are created as distinct universities with distinct hostnames
Notes: Hostnames are case-insensitive, so two tenants differing only by code case would collide on the same host

Title: Tenant switch changes the active control-plane context
Preconditions: A signed-in platform session and this run university
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/switch naming this run university; 2) Issue a control-plane read; 3) Inspect the active context
Expected Result: The response identifies the new active tenant and subsequent reads reflect it, while the estate data is unchanged
Notes: The route is observed with no documented body, response or effect. Confirm the semantics first: an undocumented switch that silently rewrites the operator tenant scope is a control-plane risk

Title: Switching to an unauthorised tenant is refused
Steps: 1) POST tenants/switch with an unknown tenant id; 2) Repeat with a tenant id the operator is not entitled to
Expected Result: 403 or 404 and the active context is unchanged
Notes: Depends on PAC-098 confirming what the switch actually does

Title: Tenant administrator cannot call the switch route
Steps: 1) Sign in on the tenant; 2) POST /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/switch from the tenant origin
Expected Result: Refused (401/403/404) and the tenant session scope is unchanged
Notes: Same origin split as 01-platform-admin.md PAC-17, applied to the write route

Title: No decommission path exists in the documented surface
Preconditions: Read access to api/endpoints/platformRoutes.ts and the console
Steps: 1) Review the observed control-plane routes and console actions; 2) Attempt DELETE on tenants/{tenantId}
Expected Result: No documented delete or decommission operation exists; DELETE is refused (404/405) and nothing is removed
Notes: Compliance reviewers need an explicit retention story. Record the absence as an observation; do not invent a delete feature

Title: Control-plane overview is readable
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/control-plane
Expected Result: 200 with the estate overview payload as JSON, and the route requires a session
Notes: The route is observed but no payload has been captured. Snapshot one response before asserting keys

Title: Invalid enum values for plan and data_region are rejected
Steps: 1) Provision with plan free-trial-xyz; 2) Provision with data_region mars-1
Expected Result: 4xx field errors and nothing created; a 2xx that stores an uninterpreted value is a defect
Notes: Values must validate against a documented list, because data_region underpins a residency claim

Title: Overview is not readable from a tenant session
Steps: 1) Sign in on the tenant; 2) GET /api/v1/enterprise/control-plane on the tenant origin and on the platform origin
Expected Result: Refused (401/403/404) on both attempts
Notes: Extends 01-platform-admin.md PAC-17 to the overview route

Title: Audit trail is readable with an explicit limit
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/control-plane/audit?limit=100
Expected Result: 200 with an array of audit entries; the default limit is 100 as built by the route helper
Notes: PlatformRouteBuilders.controlPlaneAudit() hard-codes the limit and entry fields are undocumented

Title: Provisioning is recorded in the audit trail
Steps: 1) Note the newest audit entry; 2) Provision a university; 3) Re-read the audit trail
Expected Result: A new entry records the create with actor, timestamp and the new tenant identifier
Notes: This is the primary auditability evidence for provisioning. Capture the field names before writing the assertion

Title: Password reset is recorded without the secret
Steps: 1) Reset a disposable university administrator password; 2) Read the audit trail
Expected Result: The reset is recorded with actor and tenant, and the password value never appears
Notes: An audit entry containing a password would leak a live secret into a long-lived log

Title: Audit entries are ordered newest first
Steps: 1) Perform a recorded action; 2) Read the latest audit window
Expected Result: The newest entry appears inside the returned window and timestamps are ISO-8601 and non-increasing down the list
Notes: Ordering determines whether a compliance reviewer sees the newest activity first

Title: Audit limit boundaries are handled
Steps: 1) GET the audit path with limit=0; 2) limit=-1; 3) limit=100000
Expected Result: Each is clamped or refused with a 4xx; no 5xx and no unbounded payload
Notes: Assert only that the status is below 500 and the body parses today; clamping behaviour is unverified

Title: Audit trail is append-only
Steps: 1) Attempt POST, PATCH and DELETE on the audit path
Expected Result: 405 or 404; no entry is added, changed or removed
Notes: Tamper-evident audit is the core compliance claim for a control plane

Title: Audit trail is not readable from a tenant session
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/control-plane/audit?limit=100 from the tenant origin
Notes: Estate-wide audit data would disclose every other university

Title: Institution list is readable
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/institutions
Expected Result: 200 with an array and the route requires a session
Notes: Route observed; payload undocumented

Title: An institution can be created
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/enterprise/institutions with a synthetic institution; 2) Re-read the list
Expected Result: 2xx and the institution appears exactly once in the list
Notes: The create contract is undocumented; capture the accepted body during discovery

Title: Administrator email boundary matrix
Steps: 1) Provision with admin+pac@example.com; 2) Provision with a 254-character address; 3) Provision with admin@localhost; 4) Provision with an address containing a space
Expected Result: The plus-tagged address is accepted; the over-length, domainless and space-containing addresses are refused with 4xx
Notes: This mailbox receives the one-time password, so a lenient validator sends a live secret to an undeliverable address

Title: Domain context resolves a tenant hostname
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/domain-context for that hostname
Expected Result: 200 identifying that tenant context
Notes: The route is observed with no documented parameters or payload

Title: The console host never resolves to a tenant
Steps: 1) GET domain-context for the platform host; 2) Compare with a tenant host
Expected Result: The console host resolves to the control plane and never to a tenant workspace
Notes: A console host resolving to a tenant context would blur the control-plane and tenant boundary

Title: Unknown hostname in domain context
Steps: 1) GET domain-context for unknown-runId.PLATFORM_BASE_DOMAIN
Expected Result: 404 or an explicit empty context; no fallback to another tenant
Notes: A fallback to a default tenant would be a tenant-isolation defect on every unknown host

Title: Tenant administrator cannot read the estate list
Steps: 1) Sign in on the tenant; 2) GET /api/v1/enterprise/tenants on the tenant origin
Expected Result: 401/403/404 and no estate data returned
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-17

Title: Tenant session cannot mutate another tenant
Preconditions: Tenant A administrator session and a known tenant B id
Steps: 1) PATCH /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenantB} from tenant A origin; 2) POST the reset-password path for tenant B from the same origin
Expected Result: Both are refused and tenant B is unchanged
Notes: IDOR check on the observed write routes. Re-read tenant B afterwards to prove no side effect

Title: Platform session cannot read tenant workspace APIs
Steps: 1) Request a tenant workspace route such as /api/v1/configuration/catalog on the platform origin
Expected Result: Refused; the control plane does not serve tenant workspace data
Notes: utils/platformClient.ts states that a platform token cannot call tenant routes

Title: A new tenant starts with no other tenant data
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Sign in as the new administrator; 2) Read the configuration catalog, users and marking schemes; 3) Compare the tenant id with the created tenant id
Expected Result: Only empty or provisioning-default data; the tenant id equals the created tenant id and nothing from an earlier university appears
Notes: Section 6 isolation executed on the freshly provisioned tenant; this is the strongest isolation evidence available per run

Title: Cookies are not shared across tenant hosts
Preconditions: Two universities under the same PLATFORM_BASE_DOMAIN
Steps: 1) Sign in as tenant A administrator; 2) Load tenant B host in the same context; 3) Inspect cookies and API responses
Expected Result: Tenant B does not accept tenant A session and cookies are host-scoped
Notes: Both tenants live under one base domain, so a cookie scoped to the base domain would cross tenants. Pairs with PAC-008

Title: Session identifier is replaced on sign-in
Steps: 1) Load the sign-in page and record any sessionid cookie; 2) Sign in; 3) Compare the cookie value
Expected Result: The session identifier changes after authentication
Notes: Session fixation on a control plane allows an attacker-preloaded session to become an administrative one

Title: A revoked session cannot be replayed
Steps: 1) Save the cookie; 2) Sign out; 3) Replay the saved cookie against /api/v1/enterprise/tenants
Expected Result: 401/403; the server-side session is revoked, not only the client cookie
Notes: Depends on PAC-011 confirming the console sign-out control exists

Title: Tenant list ignores unknown query parameters
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/enterprise/tenants?page=2&limit=5&unknown=1; 2) Compare with the unfiltered read
Expected Result: 200 with the same estate as the unfiltered read, or an explicit 4xx; no 5xx and no silent truncation
Notes: The route constant defines no query parameters, so an unrecognised filter must not silently drop rows

Title: A code that would shadow the console hostname is refused
Steps: 1) Provision with code platform; 2) Provision with code www
Expected Result: Refused with a 4xx explaining the reserved name, or accepted with a hostname that does not shadow the console
Notes: A tenant created on the console hostname would take over the control-plane address

Title: Empty enabled_modules list is not silently expanded
Steps: 1) Provision with enabled_modules set to an empty list; 2) Sign in as the new administrator; 3) Inspect the tenant navigation
Expected Result: The tenant is created with no optional modules, or the request is refused; it never receives every module by default
Notes: A serializer that drops an empty list would hand the tenant every module, which violates least privilege

Title: Console sign-in stays inside the expect budget
Preconditions: A provisioned environment with valid platform credentials
Steps: 1) Time sign-in from submit to the console shell; 2) Repeat three times
Expected Result: The console renders inside PLAYWRIGHT_EXPECT_TIMEOUT on all three attempts
Notes: Uses auto-waiting assertions, never a fixed sleep

Title: Provisioning latency is recorded per run
Steps: 1) Measure the create-request duration; 2) Emit it as a test annotation
Expected Result: The duration is captured on every run so a slow-provisioning trend is visible; no hard threshold beyond PLATFORM_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_MS
Notes: Annotations are the durable place for a measurement without turning it into a flaky assertion

Title: A rejected create does not corrupt the console state
Preconditions: The console open on the provisioning form
Steps: 1) Submit an invalid create; 2) Verify the estate list; 3) Provision successfully
Expected Result: No phantom row, no duplicate, and the next valid create completes
Notes: Pairs with PAC-064 by asserting the estate rather than the message

Title: Repeated failed logins behave predictably
Preconditions: A disposable platform identity; the primary operator account is never used
Steps: 1) Submit seven wrong passwords for the disposable identity; 2) Submit the correct password
Expected Result: Behaviour is either a documented lockout with a readable message or continued 401s, and the outcome is identical on repeat runs
Notes: The tenant policy documents failed_login_limit 6 and lockout_minutes 5. Whether the platform origin enforces the same limits is unverified; never test with PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAIL

Title: A long-lived session survives a bulk read
Steps: 1) Issue 100 sequential tenant-list reads; 2) Issue a create afterwards
Expected Result: No session drop and no 401 storm; the create still succeeds
Notes: Platform session timeout is unverified; the tenant policy exposes session_timeout_minutes and maximum_concurrent_sessions

Title: Rate limiting is explicit rather than silent
Steps: 1) Burst 50 invalid create attempts; 2) Read the responses
Expected Result: A clear 4xx or 429 response; no 5xx and no partial universities
Notes: Silent throttling that returns 200 with no university would be worse than a 429

Title: Sign-in controls have accessible names
Steps: 1) Inspect each input and the submit control
Expected Result: Every input has an accessible name (email and password) and the submit control is named Sign in; no unlabelled control
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-20

Title: Sign-in and provisioning are keyboard operable
Steps: 1) Tab to the email field and type; 2) Tab to the password field and type; 3) Press Enter; 4) Tab to New university and activate it with Enter or Space
Expected Result: The whole path works without a mouse and the focus order follows the visual order
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-19 asserts keyboard reachability of the sign-in controls

Title: Focus is visible on console controls
Steps: 1) Tab through the nav group, New university, the handover buttons and the tenant grid
Expected Result: Every focused control shows a visible focus indicator
Notes: Focus styling on the platform console has not been inspected

Title: Validation errors are announced
Steps: 1) Submit a duplicate code; 2) Inspect the error element and its association with the offending field
Expected Result: The error is exposed to assistive technology (alert role or live region) and is associated with the field it concerns
Notes: A screen-reader operator must be able to recover from a rejected provisioning attempt

Title: Duplicate-code error is specific and actionable
Steps: 1) Submit an existing code; 2) Read the message
Expected Result: The message names the conflicting field and tells the operator what to change
Notes: A generic request-failed message forces the operator to guess and retry, inviting duplicates

Title: Console layout holds at supported viewports
Steps: 1) At 1280x720 and 1920x1080 open Universities; 2) Activate New university
Expected Result: The primary action and the tenant grid are fully visible with no horizontal scrolling or clipped controls
Notes: Provisioning is a first-time-operator task, so a clipped primary action blocks onboarding

Title: State is not conveyed by colour alone
Preconditions: A tenant row with a status or plan indicator
Steps: 1) Inspect the row indicator
Expected Result: The state is readable as text and not only as a colour swatch
Notes: Colour-only state fails accessibility reviews and greyscale screenshots alike

Title: Console is served over HTTPS
Steps: 1) Request PLATFORM_URL; 2) Inspect the status and certificate
Expected Result: 200 with a valid certificate and no TLS error
Notes: 01-platform-admin.md PAC-21

Title: Plain HTTP is redirected or refused
Steps: 1) Request http for the console host; 2) Request http for the tenant host
Expected Result: A redirect to https or a refusal; credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP
Notes: Automation currently runs with ignoreHTTPSErrors, so TLS assertions must be run with the flag disabled to mean anything

Title: New tenant host serves a valid certificate
Preconditions: A university provisioned in this run
Steps: 1) Open the tenant URL with strict certificate checking
Expected Result: A valid certificate covering the hostname and no browser interstitial
Notes: Must be asserted with certificate validation enabled; otherwise the check is vacuous

Title: Security headers are present on the console
Steps: 1) Read the response headers of the console document
Expected Result: HSTS, a frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options policy and a nosniff content-type policy are present
Notes: Header values on the platform origin have not been captured

Title: Provisioned tenant row exists exactly once
Preconditions: A university was provisioned through POST /enterprise/tenants.
Steps: 1) Query the tenant table by tenant id and code; 2) Compare row count and key columns.
Expected Result: Exactly one row per provisioned tenant with the submitted name, code, hostname and status; no duplicate or orphan row.
Notes: Read-only control-plane DB query; table name must be captured first.

Title: University administrator row is linked to the tenant with the admin role
Preconditions: University provisioning and Admin first login completed.
Steps: 1) Query the user row by administrator email; 2) Join it to the tenant row.
Expected Result: One user row with tenant_id matching the new tenant and an administrator role; no row in another tenant.
Notes: Read-only query; role column name to be confirmed.

Title: One-time handover password is stored hashed, never plaintext
Steps: 1) Query the credential or password-hash column for the new administrator; 2) Compare with the handover value.
Expected Result: Stored value is a hash and does not equal the plaintext handover password; no plaintext copy exists.
Test Data: One-time handover password from the provisioning response
Notes: Never print the hash or the plaintext in evidence.

Title: Provisioning audit row is appended and immutable
Preconditions: A tenant was created or its administrator password was reset.
Steps: 1) Query the audit table for the actor and tenant; 2) Attempt to find an update/delete path.
Expected Result: One append-only audit row with actor, tenant, action and timestamp; no supported mutation path.
Test Data: Platform admin id and tenant id
Notes: If the control-plane audit table is not exposed, mark blocked, do not assume.

Title: 25 concurrent university provisions stay isolated
Preconditions: A disposable naming pool and write access are available.
Steps: 1) Fire 25 provisioning requests in parallel; 2) Verify each response and tenant row.
Expected Result: Each request yields a distinct tenant; no shared hostname, cross-linked administrator or partial tenant row; no 5xx.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Tenant list remains usable with 5,000 tenants
Preconditions: A seeded control-plane dataset with at least 5,000 tenants.
Steps: 1) Open or query the tenant list with pagination; 2) Measure p95 and verify page boundaries.
Expected Result: Paged results are exact and unique; p95 is within the agreed budget; no timeout or duplicate row across pages.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Audit query scales to 500,000 rows
Preconditions: An audit dataset of at least 500,000 rows.
Steps: 1) Query by actor and time range with a limit; 2) Compare returned rows with a direct count.
Expected Result: Filtering and limit are honored; p95 is within budget; total count matches the seed.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.
